<!--
PUBLICATION figure 2, the DECIDED composition (mix of 2A and 2B):

  PART A : the 5-algorithm small-multiple, for TWO parameter pairs (stacked rows)
             row 1 : (log10 k_on, log10 k_off)        kinetic axis
             row 2 : (log10 N_ch, log10 i_unit)       amplitude axis (N*i ridge)
           Shows the failures: for NR/MNR/R/MR the empirical mean drifts off truth
           (bias) and the naive Fisher ellipse mis-sizes the cloud (mis-calibration).

  PART B : the FULL correlation corner of the four informative parameters
             (on, off, unitary_current, Num_ch_mean) for MacroIR ALONE.
           Shows the success in full: in every parameter pair the three ellipses
           (empirical / Fisher / corrected) coincide (second-moment calibration) AND
           the three centre markers (truth / empirical mean / predicted truth+DIB)
           coincide on the truth (first-moment / unbiasedness). MR corner dropped.

Anchoring/scaling identical to figure_2_pub.Rmd: model covariances at theta_pool
(*_battery_pool), cov_scale = 1/REP_GROUP. group_size = 10, noise = 0.1.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
```

```{r params}
# ---- which Fisher anchors the ellipses -------------------------------------------------
# "gaussian" is the anchor the paper promises (papers/1_method/00_plan.md section 6) AND the only
# basis macro_VR can ever join, because VR is dispatched by dispatch_figure_3_G.sh alone.
# "numeric" is the legacy finite-difference basis: five algorithms, no VR, kept because the
# agreement between the two is itself a reported result.
#
# THE TWO ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE BY PATH. The Gaussian files carry BOTH vocabularies, and the
# legacy `Likelihood_*` components are present there with bootstrap_count rows and NO value rows.
# Repointing DATA_DIR without also switching the component prefix therefore drops every ellipse
# and renders an empty figure with no error. Verified 2026-07-21 on macro_MR at this cell:
# Likelihood_Fisher_Covariance has 7 bootstrap_count rows and 0 value rows in the Gaussian file,
# against 1512 value rows in the numeric one.
ANCHOR <- "gaussian"

# DATA_DIRS is a SEARCH PATH, not one folder. The dispatcher isolates output per engine commit, so
# an algorithm added later lands in its own hash directory (macro_VR is in 0ffbda7, the rest of the
# Gaussian grid in 1c2ae6f). Mixing them in one panel is sanctioned: D-0 accepted multi-commit
# provenance because every CSV stamps its own engine hash in row 1, so the folder name is a scratch
# grouping and the FILE is the provenance record. Each algorithm resolves to the first directory
# holding a complete set for it.
if (ANCHOR == "gaussian") {
  DATA_DIRS <- c("../data/a202e03", "../data/1f7138b", "../data/1c2ae6f", "../data/0ffbda7", "../data/87889e6")
  FILE_PRE <- "figure_3_G_"; BAT_SUF <- "_G"; COMP_PRE <- "Gaussian_"
} else if (ANCHOR == "numeric") {
  DATA_DIRS <- "../data/433ed13"
  FILE_PRE <- "figure_3_";   BAT_SUF <- "";   COMP_PRE <- "Likelihood_"
} else stop("ANCHOR must be 'gaussian' or 'numeric'")

C_FISHER    <- paste0(COMP_PRE, "Fisher_Covariance")
C_CORRECTED <- paste0(COMP_PRE, "Distortion_Corrected_Covariance")
C_BIAS      <- paste0(COMP_PRE, "Distortion_Induced_Bias")

REP_NCH      <- 100
REP_NSIM     <- 10000
REP_NOISE    <- "0.1"
REP_GROUP    <- 10
REP_INTERVAL <- 0.1

# A-strict roster: paper 1 measures the recursive ladder only (papers/1_method/decisions.md).
# VR is listed here on purpose. It has no battery/cloud data at any anchor yet, so it is dropped
# below WITH A MESSAGE rather than silently; the day the grid run lands it appears by itself.
# the full seven-rung ladder; LSE resolves from its own file prefix (see .pre below)
# macro_INR, not macro_NMR: the latter is the build that lost the N*ms term between a3e0a89 and
# 1f7138b and is a different algorithm, not an older spelling (nomenclature.md). 1f7138b leads the
# search path so the corrected member resolves from the run made for this figure.
# EIGHT columns since 2026-08-06: the un-averaged least-squares arm landed at this cell. The two
# arms are ONE flag apart (dispatch_figure_3_LSE.sh:144-146): nonlinearsqr is averaging=1 (ILSE) and
# nonlinearsqr_g is averaging=0 (LSE), family=2 for both. nonlinearsqr_g resolves from a202e03, the
# commit that corrected the av=0 fold; that correction is av=0 ONLY, so no other column moves.
ROSTER   <- c("nonlinearsqr_g","nonlinearsqr","macro_NR","macro_INR","macro_R","macro_MR","macro_VR","macro_IR")
# NMR and INR are two DIFFERENT algorithms, not two spellings: NMR is the build that lost the
# N*ms term between a3e0a89 and 1f7138b, INR is the corrected one (nomenclature.md). Both keys
# stay so the readers can tell them apart; the ROSTER above says which one is drawn.
ALGO_LAB <- c(nonlinearsqr_g="LSE", nonlinearsqr="ILSE", macro_NR="NR", macro_NMR="NMR", macro_INR="INR",
              macro_R="R", macro_MR="MR", macro_VR="VR", macro_IR="IR")

PARAM_IDX <- c(on = 0, off = 1, unitary_current = 2, Current_Noise = 3, Num_ch_mean = 5)
# plotmath-parseable labels (rendered as proper subscripted math on axes and strips)
PARAM_LAB <- c(on = "log[10]~k[on]", off = "log[10]~k[off]",
               unitary_current = "log[10]~i", Current_Noise = "log[10]~sigma",
               Num_ch_mean = "log[10]~N[ch]")
ORD <- c("on","off","unitary_current","Num_ch_mean")
TRUTH <- c(on = log10(10), off = log10(100),
           unitary_current = log10(1), Current_Noise = log10(as.numeric(REP_NOISE)/1000),
           Num_ch_mean = log10(REP_NCH))

cov_scale <- 1 / REP_GROUP
near_int  <- function(x) abs(x - REP_INTERVAL) < 1e-9
```

```{r read}
read_skip1 <- function(path) read.csv(path, skip = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
# LSE (nonlinearsqr) has its OWN dispatcher (dispatch_figure_3_LSE.sh) with its own file prefix
# figure_3_LSE_; the macro/Gaussian grid uses FILE_PRE. Per-algo prefix so the LSE column resolves
# from its own files while NR/R/IR resolve from the Gaussian ones. Its battery still carries the
# Gaussian_ components and the _G suffix, so COMP_PRE / BAT_SUF are unchanged.
.pre    <- function(a) if (startsWith(a, "nonlinearsqr")) "figure_3_LSE_" else FILE_PRE
.stem   <- function(dir, a) file.path(dir,
  sprintf("%snch_%d_nsim_%d_%s_noise_%s", .pre(a), REP_NCH, REP_NSIM, a, REP_NOISE))
.needed <- function(stem) paste0(stem, c("_mle_cloud_runs.csv",
                                         paste0("_battery_pool", BAT_SUF, ".csv"),
                                         paste0("_battery_sim",  BAT_SUF, ".csv")))
# first directory of the search path holding a COMPLETE set for this algorithm, else NA
base_for <- function(a) {
  for (d in DATA_DIRS) { st <- .stem(d, a); if (all(file.exists(.needed(st)))) return(st) }
  NA_character_
}

# no silent drops: an algorithm with no complete set is named out loud and removed
have <- vapply(ROSTER, function(a) !is.na(base_for(a)), logical(1))
# cat(), not message(): the setup chunk sets message = FALSE, which would swallow it, and the
# whole point of this line is that a missing algorithm can never pass unnoticed.
if (!all(have)) cat("figure_2: INCOMPLETE at anchor '", ANCHOR, "', dropped from the figure: ",
                    paste(ROSTER[!have], collapse = ", "),
                    "\n           (a cloud alone is not enough: the ellipses need ",
                    "_battery_pool", BAT_SUF, " and the bias marker _battery_sim", BAT_SUF, ")\n", sep = "")
if (!any(have)) stop("figure_2: no algorithm of the roster has a complete set under ",
                     paste(DATA_DIRS, collapse = ", "))
ALGOS   <- ROSTER[have]
ALGO_LV <- unname(ALGO_LAB[ALGOS])      # factor levels: only the columns actually drawn
base    <- vapply(ALGOS, base_for, character(1))
cat("figure_2: drawing", paste(ALGO_LAB[ALGOS], collapse = ", "), "from\n",
    paste0("  ", ALGOS, " <- ", dirname(base), collapse = "\n"), "\n")

cloud   <- map_dfr(paste0(base, "_mle_cloud_runs.csv"), read_skip1)
battery <- map_dfr(paste0(base, "_battery_pool", BAT_SUF, ".csv"), read_skip1) %>%
  mutate(component = str_replace(component_path, "^Probit_statistics_", ""))
bsim    <- map_dfr(paste0(base, "_battery_sim", BAT_SUF, ".csv"), read_skip1) %>%
  mutate(component = str_replace(component_path, "^Probit_statistics_", ""),
         algo = factor(ALGO_LAB[algorithm], levels = ALGO_LV))

pts <- cloud %>%
  filter(component_path == "Model_Parameters_Hat", statistic == "value",
         Num_ch == REP_NCH, group_size == REP_GROUP, near_int(interval_in_tau),
         param_name %in% names(PARAM_IDX)) %>%
  select(algorithm, sample_index, param_name, value) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = param_name, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(algo = factor(ALGO_LAB[algorithm], levels = ALGO_LV))
```

```{r helpers}
# breaks ANCHORED on the centre (the expected value, a round 0/1/2) with a 1-2-5 nice
# step: the round value always gets a tick AND there are enough ticks (3-5) to read the scale.
centered_break_vec <- function(center, half) {
  if (!is.finite(half) || half <= 0) return(center)
  # 3 ticks (centre and one each side). Pick the LARGEST "nice" step (1-2-4-5 ladder) that still
  # fits inside the half-width, so the two outer ticks sit as close to the panel edge as possible
  # without being clipped. The old 0.6*half heuristic undershot wide panels (the log10 N_ch axis
  # ended at +/-0.46 but the outer ticks landed at +/-0.2, leaving the ends bare -> "missing 1.6 /
  # 2.4"). Including 4*mag lets that axis snap to a 0.4 step -> ticks 1.6 / 2.0 / 2.4.
  mag  <- 10^floor(log10(half))
  cand <- c(1, 2, 4, 5) * mag; cand <- c(cand, cand * 10)
  step <- max(cand[cand <= half])
  # SNAP the centre onto the tick grid so the middle tick is a ROUND value, even when `center` is a
  # data mean(lims) pulled off the round truth by asymmetric outliers (that gave ticks like 2.000974).
  center <- round(center / step) * step
  round(center + step * (-1:1), 6)   # 3 ROUND ticks centred on the (snapped) expected value
}
# free-scale facets (corner): each panel is symmetric about its truth, so centre = mean(lims)
sym_breaks_fn <- function(lims) centered_break_vec(mean(lims), (max(lims) - min(lims)) / 2)

ellipse_path <- function(cx, cy, S, level = 0.95, npoints = 200) {
  if (is.null(S) || any(!is.finite(S))) return(NULL)
  ev <- eigen(S, symmetric = TRUE)
  if (any(ev$values <= 0)) return(NULL)
  r  <- sqrt(qchisq(level, df = 2))
  th <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = npoints)
  Tm <- ev$vectors %*% diag(sqrt(ev$values)) %*% t(ev$vectors)
  P  <- Tm %*% (r * rbind(cos(th), sin(th)))
  data.frame(x = cx + P[1, ], y = cy + P[2, ])
}

# ellipse "area" proxy = sqrt(det) (proportional to the 95% region area); ratios grade each ellipse
.area <- function(S) if (is.null(S) || any(!is.finite(S))) NA_real_ else
  { ev <- eigen(S, symmetric = TRUE)$values; if (any(ev <= 0)) NA_real_ else sqrt(prod(ev)) }
.fmt  <- function(r) ifelse(!is.finite(r), "", ifelse(r >= 10, sprintf("%.0f×", r), sprintf("%.1f×", r)))

# THE SHAPE COMPANION TO .area(), and the two of them are an exact decomposition rather than two
# summaries that happen to sit together. With M = S_F^{-1/2} S_emp S_F^{-1/2} and its eigenvalues
# lambda_1 >= lambda_2, the area ratio this figure ALREADY prints is sqrt(lambda_1 * lambda_2), which
# is exp(mean(log lambda)); the orthogonal companion is sqrt(lambda_1/lambda_2), which is
# exp(sd(log lambda)). So the pair on every panel is exactly the pair the anisotropy map carries over
# the whole design plane (Figure 4--figure supplement, magnitude/anisotropy), restricted to this 2D
# slice. The first says by how much the report is wrong; the second says whether ONE factor could
# repair it, which is the correction a reader reaches for and the one this paper says does not exist.
#
# A 2D slice is a LOWER BOUND on the anisotropy of the full six-parameter object: a pair can look
# round while the matrix is strongly anisotropic in a direction that mixes parameters. The caption
# says so, and it is why the map figure is not made redundant by these numbers.
.shape <- function(Semp, SF) {
  if (is.null(Semp) || is.null(SF) || any(!is.finite(Semp)) || any(!is.finite(SF)))
    return(NA_real_)
  ev <- tryCatch(Re(eigen(solve(SF, Semp), only.values = TRUE)$values),
                 error = function(e) NA_real_)
  if (any(!is.finite(ev)) || any(ev <= 0)) return(NA_real_)
  sqrt(max(ev) / min(ev))
}
# printed as a spread, not as a factor, so it cannot be read as "multiply by this"
# WRITTEN IN PARENTHESES, 2026-08-12. The pair printed as "15× ×÷1.4" put two multiplication signs
# side by side with only a space between them, which on the page reads as one garbled symbol. The
# parenthesis separates them and costs two characters.
.fmts <- function(r) ifelse(!is.finite(r), "", sprintf("(×÷%.1f)", r))

battery_cov_pair <- function(comp, algo, ix, jx) {           # ix,jx = param indices
  df <- battery %>%
    filter(component == comp, statistic == "value", probit == "mean",
           algorithm == algo, Num_ch == REP_NCH, near_int(interval_in_tau),
           param_index %in% c(ix, jx), param_col %in% c(ix, jx)) %>%
    select(param_index, param_col, value)
  m <- matrix(NA_real_, 2, 2); idx <- c(ix, jx)
  for (a in 1:2) for (b in 1:2) {
    v <- df$value[df$param_index == idx[a] & df$param_col == idx[b]]
    if (length(v) == 1 && is.finite(v)) m[a, b] <- v
  }
  m * cov_scale
}

# DIB vector (named param -> bias) for one algorithm, from battery_sim
dib_vector <- function(algo) {
  bsim %>%
    filter(component == C_BIAS, statistic == "value",
           probit == "mean", algorithm == .env$algo, Num_ch == REP_NCH,
           near_int(interval_in_tau), param_name %in% ORD) %>%
    select(param_name, value) %>% deframe()
}

# --- PART A: 5-algorithm small-multiple for one parameter pair ---
centers_for_pair <- function(px, py, algos) {
  dib <- bsim %>%
    filter(component == C_BIAS, statistic == "value",
           probit == "mean", Num_ch == REP_NCH, near_int(interval_in_tau),
           param_name %in% c(px, py)) %>%
    select(algo, param_name, value) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = param_name, values_from = value)
  truth <- tibble(algo = factor(ALGO_LAB[algos], levels = ALGO_LV),
                  x = unname(TRUTH[px]), y = unname(TRUTH[py]), kind = "truth")
  empc <- pts %>% filter(algorithm %in% algos) %>% group_by(algo) %>%
    summarise(x = mean(.data[[px]], na.rm = TRUE),
              y = mean(.data[[py]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(kind = "empirical mean")
  predc <- dib %>%
    transmute(algo, x = unname(TRUTH[px]) + .data[[px]],
              y = unname(TRUTH[py]) + .data[[py]], kind = "predicted (truth + bias)")
  bind_rows(truth, empc, predc) %>%
    mutate(kind = factor(kind, levels = c("truth","empirical mean","predicted (truth + bias)")))
}

pair_plot <- function(px, py, algos = ALGOS) {
  pix <- PARAM_IDX[px]; piy <- PARAM_IDX[py]
  cl_all <- pts %>% filter(algorithm %in% algos) %>%
    transmute(algo, x = .data[[px]], y = .data[[py]]) %>% filter(is.finite(x), is.finite(y))
  ell <- list()
  for (a in algos) {
    cl <- pts %>% filter(algorithm == a) %>%
      transmute(x = .data[[px]], y = .data[[py]]) %>% filter(is.finite(x), is.finite(y))
    if (nrow(cl) < 3) next
    ctr  <- c(mean(cl$x), mean(cl$y))
    Ss <- list(empirical = cov(cbind(cl$x, cl$y)),
               Fisher    = battery_cov_pair(C_FISHER, a, pix, piy),
               corrected = battery_cov_pair(C_CORRECTED, a, pix, piy))
    # THE BEST A SINGLE FACTOR CAN DO: the Fisher ellipse resized to the empirical AREA, and nothing
    # else touched. If the distortion were a scalar, which is the effective-N rescaling a reader
    # reaches for and which the integrated autocorrelation would supply, this curve would land ON the
    # empirical one. Where it does not, no rescaling reaches, and the gap the eye sees IS the shape
    # number in the corner. Scaling a 2x2 by k scales its area by k, so k is the ratio of areas.
    if (!is.null(Ss$Fisher) && all(is.finite(Ss$Fisher))) {
      k <- .area(Ss$empirical) / .area(Ss$Fisher)
      if (is.finite(k) && k > 0) Ss[["Fisher rescaled"]] <- Ss$Fisher * k
    }
    for (nm in names(Ss)) {
      e <- ellipse_path(ctr[1], ctr[2], Ss[[nm]])
      if (!is.null(e)) ell[[length(ell) + 1]] <- e %>% mutate(algo = ALGO_LAB[a], source = nm)
    }
  }
  ellipses <- bind_rows(ell) %>%
    mutate(algo = factor(algo, levels = ALGO_LV),
           source = factor(source, levels = c("empirical","Fisher","Fisher rescaled","corrected")))
  centers <- centers_for_pair(px, py, algos)
  tx <- unname(TRUTH[px]); ty <- unname(TRUTH[py])     # centre EVERY panel on the expected value
  hx <- 1.25 * max(abs(quantile(cl_all$x, c(.01, .99), na.rm = TRUE) - tx))
  hy <- 1.25 * max(abs(quantile(cl_all$y, c(.01, .99), na.rm = TRUE) - ty))
  xb <- centered_break_vec(tx, hx); yb <- centered_break_vec(ty, hy)

  # per-facet area-ratio labels: empirical/Fisher (the overconfidence factor) and empirical/corrected
  # (~1 when the sandwich recovers the true spread). Each number is coloured like the ellipse it grades.
  labs_df <- map_dfr(algos, function(a) {
    cl <- pts %>% filter(algorithm == a) %>%
      transmute(x = .data[[px]], y = .data[[py]]) %>% filter(is.finite(x), is.finite(y))
    if (nrow(cl) < 3) return(NULL)
    Aemp <- .area(cov(cbind(cl$x, cl$y)))
    # LABELS OUT OF THE DATA, 2026-08-12. They used to sit inside the panel, in whichever top corner
    # was off the cloud's tilt, and in the k_off row the widest clouds reach BOTH top corners: the
    # LSE and ILSE numbers were clipped by the panel edge and drawn over their own ellipse (same in
    # the N_ch row for NR). They now live in a band above the data that the y expansion opens, one
    # text row instead of two, orange at the left edge and blue at the right, so no tilt rule is
    # needed and nothing can collide with the cloud whatever its shape. TWO ROWS, not one: at 7 pt in
    # a 0.74 in panel the three numbers do not fit on a line, and putting them on one had them
    # overprinting each other, which is worse than what it fixed.
    SF <- battery_cov_pair(C_FISHER, a, pix, piy)
    # size and shape on ONE line. They are one decomposition and reading them as a pair is the whole
    # point; stacking them also cost a third text row, which pushed the blue number down into the
    # cloud in the panels whose ellipses are widest.
    tibble(algo  = factor(ALGO_LAB[a], levels = ALGO_LV),
           lab_F = paste(.fmt(Aemp / .area(SF)),
                         .fmts(.shape(cov(cbind(cl$x, cl$y)), SF))),
           lab_C = .fmt(Aemp / .area(battery_cov_pair(C_CORRECTED, a, pix, piy))))
  }) %>% mutate(x  = tx - hx * 0.99,
                yF = ty + hy * (1 + 2 * YPAD * 0.78),    # top row of the band, orange
                yC = ty + hy * (1 + 2 * YPAD * 0.30))    # second row, blue; vjust=1 hangs each below
  # DROPPED HALF A TEXT LINE, 2026-08-12: at 0.98 the orange row sat on the panel's top border, a
  # hair under the facet strip. Half a line is 0.137 hy here (0.055 in against a 0.403 in hy), which
  # is 0.20 of the band, so both rows moved by 0.20 and their spacing is unchanged.

  ggplot() +
    geom_point(data = cl_all, aes(x, y), colour = "grey55", size = .35, alpha = .18) +
    geom_path(data = ellipses, aes(x, y, colour = source, linetype = source, linewidth = source)) +
    geom_point(data = centers, aes(x, y, shape = kind), size = 2.4, stroke = .9,
               colour = "black", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_text(data = labs_df, aes(x, yF, label = lab_F), hjust = 0, colour = "#D55E00",
              size = 2.8, vjust = 1) +
    geom_text(data = labs_df, aes(x, yC, label = lab_C), hjust = 0, colour = "#0072B2",
              size = 2.8, vjust = 1) +
    facet_wrap(~ algo, nrow = 1) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = tx + c(-hx, hx), ylim = ty + c(-hy, hy)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = xb) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = yb, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, YPAD))) +
    # "Fisher rescaled" takes the Fisher COLOUR because it is the Fisher ellipse, with the single
    # degree of freedom a scalar correction has already spent in its favour. Its own dash pattern,
    # and thin, so it reads as a construction and not as a fourth estimate of the covariance.
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(empirical = "grey45", Fisher = "#D55E00",
                                   `Fisher rescaled` = "#D55E00",
                                   corrected = "#0072B2"), name = NULL) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(empirical = "solid", Fisher = "dashed",
                                     `Fisher rescaled` = "dotdash",
                                     corrected = "dotted"), name = NULL) +
    scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(empirical = .55, Fisher = .75,
                                      `Fisher rescaled` = .5, corrected = 1.05), guide = "none") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("truth" = 3, "empirical mean" = 19,
                                  "predicted (truth + bias)" = 1), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = parse(text = unname(PARAM_LAB[px]))[[1]],
         y = parse(text = unname(PARAM_LAB[py]))[[1]]) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}

# --- PART B: full lower-triangle correlation corner for ONE algorithm,
#             with ellipses (emp/Fisher/corrected) AND markers (truth/emp/pred) ---
corner_plot <- function(algo, title = NULL) {
  xlev <- ORD[1:3]; ylev <- ORD[2:4]
  prs <- expand.grid(xp = ORD, yp = ORD, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    filter(match(yp, ORD) > match(xp, ORD))
  cl  <- pts %>% filter(algorithm == .env$algo)          # .env: arg wins over `algo` column
  dib <- dib_vector(algo)

  cloud_l <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(prs)), function(k) {
    xp <- prs$xp[k]; yp <- prs$yp[k]
    cl %>% transmute(xp = xp, yp = yp, x = .data[[xp]], y = .data[[yp]])
  }) %>% filter(is.finite(x), is.finite(y))

  ell_l <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(prs)), function(k) {
    xp <- prs$xp[k]; yp <- prs$yp[k]
    c2 <- cl %>% transmute(x = .data[[xp]], y = .data[[yp]]) %>% filter(is.finite(x), is.finite(y))
    if (nrow(c2) < 3) return(NULL)
    ctr <- c(mean(c2$x), mean(c2$y))
    Ss <- list(empirical = cov(cbind(c2$x, c2$y)),
               Fisher    = battery_cov_pair(C_FISHER, algo, PARAM_IDX[xp], PARAM_IDX[yp]),
               corrected = battery_cov_pair(C_CORRECTED, algo, PARAM_IDX[xp], PARAM_IDX[yp]))
    map_dfr(names(Ss), function(nm) {
      e <- ellipse_path(ctr[1], ctr[2], Ss[[nm]]); if (is.null(e)) return(NULL)
      e %>% mutate(xp = xp, yp = yp, source = nm)
    })
  })

  cen_l <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(prs)), function(k) {
    xpk <- prs$xp[k]; ypk <- prs$yp[k]
    c2 <- cl %>% transmute(x = .data[[xpk]], y = .data[[ypk]]) %>% filter(is.finite(x), is.finite(y))
    # precompute scalars OUTSIDE tibble() so its data-masking cannot reinterpret xp/yp as the
    # just-created columns (the bug that inflated column sizes)
    tx <- unname(TRUTH[xpk]); ty <- unname(TRUTH[ypk])
    bx <- unname(dib[xpk]);   by <- unname(dib[ypk])
    mx <- if (nrow(c2)) mean(c2$x) else NA_real_
    my <- if (nrow(c2)) mean(c2$y) else NA_real_
    tibble(xp = xpk, yp = ypk,
           x = c(tx, mx, tx + bx),
           y = c(ty, my, ty + by),
           kind = c("truth", "empirical mean", "predicted (truth + bias)"))
  })

  fx <- function(z) factor(z, levels = xlev, labels = unname(PARAM_LAB[xlev]))
  fy <- function(z) factor(z, levels = ylev, labels = unname(PARAM_LAB[ylev]))
  cloud_l <- mutate(cloud_l, xp = fx(xp), yp = fy(yp))
  ell_l   <- mutate(ell_l,   xp = fx(xp), yp = fy(yp),
                    source = factor(source, levels = c("empirical","Fisher","corrected")))
  cen_l   <- mutate(cen_l,   xp = fx(xp), yp = fy(yp),
                    kind = factor(kind, levels = c("truth","empirical mean","predicted (truth + bias)")))

  # symmetric per-panel limits so the expected value sits at the CENTRE of each cell; the extra
  # half-width (1.25) also leaves clean room for the area-ratio labels in the top-left corner.
  lims_l <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(prs)), function(k) {
    xpk <- prs$xp[k]; ypk <- prs$yp[k]
    c2 <- cl %>% transmute(x = .data[[xpk]], y = .data[[ypk]]) %>% filter(is.finite(x), is.finite(y))
    tx <- unname(TRUTH[xpk]); ty <- unname(TRUTH[ypk])
    hx <- 1.25 * max(abs(quantile(c2$x, c(.01, .99), na.rm = TRUE) - tx))
    hy <- 1.25 * max(abs(quantile(c2$y, c(.01, .99), na.rm = TRUE) - ty))
    tibble(xp = xpk, yp = ypk, x = c(tx - hx, tx + hx), y = c(ty - hy, ty + hy))
  }) %>% mutate(xp = fx(xp), yp = fy(yp))
  # clip the cloud to the symmetric [truth +/- h] panel so the TRUTH stays CENTRED in every cell
  # (outlier points would otherwise drag the free-scale range off-centre and un-round the ticks).
  .bnd <- lims_l %>% group_by(xp, yp) %>%
    summarise(x0 = min(x), x1 = max(x), y0 = min(y), y1 = max(y), .groups = "drop")
  cloud_l <- cloud_l %>% inner_join(.bnd, by = c("xp", "yp")) %>%
    filter(x >= x0, x <= x1, y >= y0, y <= y1) %>% select(-x0, -x1, -y0, -y1)

  # area-ratio labels per corner cell (same convention as Part A): orange = empirical/Fisher,
  # blue = empirical/corrected. For IR they are ~1x everywhere, the quantitative face of "IR calibrates".
  labs_l <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(prs)), function(k) {
    xpk <- prs$xp[k]; ypk <- prs$yp[k]
    c2 <- cl %>% transmute(x = .data[[xpk]], y = .data[[ypk]]) %>% filter(is.finite(x), is.finite(y))
    if (nrow(c2) < 3) return(NULL)
    tx <- unname(TRUTH[xpk]); ty <- unname(TRUTH[ypk])
    hx <- 1.25 * max(abs(quantile(c2$x, c(.01, .99), na.rm = TRUE) - tx)); hy <- 1.25 * max(abs(quantile(c2$y, c(.01, .99), na.rm = TRUE) - ty))
    Aemp <- .area(cov(cbind(c2$x, c2$y)))
    # place the labels in the TOP corner OFF the cloud's tilt: positive correlation -> the cloud
    # runs bottom-left..top-right, so top-left is empty (hj=0); negative -> top-right is empty (hj=1).
    rho <- suppressWarnings(cor(c2$x, c2$y))
    hj  <- if (is.finite(rho) && rho < 0) 1 else 0
    SFk <- battery_cov_pair(C_FISHER, algo, PARAM_IDX[xpk], PARAM_IDX[ypk])
    # the shape number rides here too: for IR it is the quantitative face of "IR calibrates" extended
    # from size to shape, which is the stronger of the two statements and the one Part A's failing
    # members do not get. No rescaled curve in the corner: fifteen cells cannot carry a fourth path.
    tibble(xp = xpk, yp = ypk, hj = hj,
           lab_F = paste(.fmt(Aemp / .area(SFk)),
                         .fmts(.shape(cov(cbind(c2$x, c2$y)), SFk))),
           lab_C = .fmt(Aemp / .area(battery_cov_pair(C_CORRECTED, algo, PARAM_IDX[xpk], PARAM_IDX[ypk]))),
           x = tx + ifelse(hj == 1, hx, -hx) * 0.92, yF = ty + hy * 0.92, yC = ty + hy * 0.60)
  }) %>% mutate(xp = fx(xp), yp = fy(yp))

  ggplot() +
    geom_blank(data = lims_l, aes(x, y)) +
    geom_point(data = cloud_l, aes(x, y), colour = "grey55", size = .3, alpha = .15) +
    geom_path(data = ell_l, aes(x, y, colour = source, linetype = source, linewidth = source)) +
    geom_point(data = cen_l, aes(x, y, shape = kind), size = 2, stroke = .8,
               colour = "black", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_text(data = labs_l, aes(x, yF, label = lab_F, hjust = hj), colour = "#D55E00", size = 2.8, vjust = 1) +
    geom_text(data = labs_l, aes(x, yC, label = lab_C, hjust = hj), colour = "#0072B2", size = 2.8, vjust = 1) +
    facet_grid(yp ~ xp, scales = "free", drop = FALSE, labeller = label_parsed) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = sym_breaks_fn) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = sym_breaks_fn) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(empirical = "grey45", Fisher = "#D55E00",
                                   corrected = "#0072B2"), name = NULL) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(empirical = "solid", Fisher = "dashed",
                                     corrected = "dotted"), name = NULL) +
    scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(empirical = .5, Fisher = .65, corrected = .95), guide = "none") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("truth" = 3, "empirical mean" = 19,
                                  "predicted (truth + bias)" = 1), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = title) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_text(size = 9),
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11, face = "bold"))
}
```

```{r plot}
library(grid)
# Figure 2 is Part A only: the seven-rung ladder across the columns, one parameter pair per row.
# The corner (Part B) moved out of the body figure; corner_plot() above still builds it for the
# supplement. Layout rule: the panel size is MEASURED, not guessed. Panel width follows from the
# column count and the plot's own non-panel width; each row's height is then that width (square
# panels) plus that row's own overhead. Nothing is centred, so no white gaps appear.
W <- 7.0

# Non-panel space is panel space not spent: strips, tick labels, ticks and axis titles all run
# small so the panels keep what is freed.
# eLife requires every character to be at least 7 pt AT FINAL PRINTED SIZE. That floor is an input
# to the layout, not a polish step: the panel size below is whatever the width leaves once the axis
# labels, tick labels, strips and axis titles have taken theirs, so the type sizes are set first and
# the panels take what is left. Authored at 7 pt, not at 6.6 relying on the 6.1% enlargement that
# \includegraphics[width=\linewidth] applies inside fullwidth: an explicit width would break that.
PT <- 7
# Y HEADROOM AND PANEL ASPECT, 2026-08-12. YPAD is the fraction of the full y range added ABOVE the
# data, where the two ratio labels now live; the data band itself is unchanged, so the truth stays at
# the centre of the DATA and only the axis grows. ASPECT then makes the panel taller by the same
# amount, so opening that band costs the cloud none of its height on the page.
YPAD   <- 0.34
# ASPECT compensates the band. At 1 + 2*YPAD it gives the cloud MORE height than it had before the
# band existed (0.90 in against 0.70), and the float then does not fit its caption on the page. 1.50
# leaves the cloud at 0.80 in, still taller than the square panels it replaces, and takes 0.4 in off
# the figure.
ASPECT <- 1.50
DIET <- theme(panel.spacing.x = unit(6, "pt"), panel.spacing.y = unit(4, "pt"),
              plot.margin = margin(1, 1, 1, 1),
              axis.text = element_text(size = PT), axis.title = element_text(size = PT),
              axis.ticks.length = unit(1.4, "pt"),
              legend.text = element_text(size = PT),
              strip.text = element_text(size = PT, margin = margin(1.2, 1.2, 1.2, 1.2)))

# BOTH least-squares arms hold the unitary current and the noise level Fixed AT THE SIMULATED
# VALUES, so neither has a cloud in any pair that involves them: their estimates would sit exactly
# on a line and the area ratio the panel reports would be 0/0. The cells stay, to keep the columns
# aligned, and say so. Four such cells since the av=0 arm joined, two per least-squares column.
LSE_ARMS <- intersect(c("nonlinearsqr_g", "nonlinearsqr"), ALGOS)
NOLSE <- setdiff(ALGOS, LSE_ARMS)
note_cell <- function(px, py, lab) {
  d <- data.frame(algo = factor(unname(ALGO_LAB[LSE_ARMS]), levels = ALGO_LV),
                  x = unname(TRUTH[px]), y = unname(TRUTH[py]))
  geom_text(data = d, aes(x = x, y = y), label = lab, size = PT/.pt, colour = "grey45",
            lineheight = 1.05, inherit.aes = FALSE)
}

r1 <- pair_plot("on", "off", ALGOS) + labs(tag = "A") + DIET
r2 <- pair_plot("Num_ch_mean", "unitary_current", NOLSE) +
      note_cell("Num_ch_mean", "unitary_current", "i fixed\nat the truth") + DIET
r3 <- pair_plot("Current_Noise", "Num_ch_mean", NOLSE) +
      note_cell("Current_Noise", "Num_ch_mean", "sigma fixed\nat the truth") + DIET

geom_of <- function(p) {
  g <- ggplotGrob(p); pr <- grep("^panel", g$layout$name)
  rr <- sort(unique(g$layout$t[pr])); cc <- sort(unique(g$layout$l[pr]))
  list(nr = length(rr), nc = length(cc),
       oh = sum(convertHeight(g$heights[-rr], "in", valueOnly = TRUE)),
       ow = sum(convertWidth(g$widths[-cc], "in", valueOnly = TRUE)))
}
gm <- lapply(list(r1, r2, r3), function(p) geom_of(p + theme(legend.position = "none")))
pw <- (W - gm[[1]]$ow) / gm[[1]]$nc                       # panel WIDTH, in inches

g2 <- (r1 / r2 / r3) +
  plot_layout(heights = unit(vapply(gm, function(z) pw * ASPECT + z$oh, 0), "in"), guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "horizontal", legend.title = element_blank(),
        legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0), legend.spacing.x = unit(5, "pt"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = PT), legend.key.size = unit(10, "pt"))
H <- sum(convertHeight(patchwork::patchworkGrob(g2)$heights, "in", valueOnly = TRUE))
cat(sprintf("figure_2: panel %.3f x %.3f in, figure %.2f x %.2f in\n", pw, pw * ASPECT, W, H))
g2
ggsave("Figure_2.pdf", g2, width = W, height = H)
```

```{r diagnostics-table}
area <- function(S) if (is.null(S) || any(!is.finite(S))) NA else
  { ev <- eigen(S, symmetric = TRUE)$values; if (any(ev <= 0)) NA else sqrt(prod(ev)) }

# Part A pairs: Fisher/empirical ratio per algorithm (overconfidence > 1 means Fisher too tight)
diag_pair <- function(px, py) {
  pix <- PARAM_IDX[px]; piy <- PARAM_IDX[py]
  map_dfr(ALGOS, function(a) {
    cl <- pts %>% filter(algorithm == a) %>%
      transmute(x = .data[[px]], y = .data[[py]]) %>% filter(is.finite(x), is.finite(y))
    Semp <- if (nrow(cl) > 2) cov(cbind(cl$x, cl$y)) else NULL
    tibble(pair = paste(px, py, sep = "/"), algorithm = ALGO_LAB[a],
           empirical = area(Semp),
           Fisher    = area(battery_cov_pair(C_FISHER, a, pix, piy)),
           corrected = area(battery_cov_pair(C_CORRECTED, a, pix, piy))) %>%
      mutate(emp_over_Fisher = empirical / Fisher)
  })
}
bind_rows(diag_pair("on", "off"), diag_pair("Num_ch_mean", "unitary_current"),
          diag_pair("Current_Noise", "Num_ch_mean"))

# IR unbiasedness check: empirical mean - truth per param (should be ~0)
pts %>% filter(algorithm == "macro_IR") %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(ORD), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "param", values_to = "emp_mean") %>%
  mutate(truth = unname(TRUTH[param]), bias = emp_mean - truth)
```
